blockingFindings.description: The acceptance suite reports ALL six checks as failed, but this is caused by a defect in the test's OWN helper (paintCell), not by the application. The helper calls Breakout.clearGrid() on every invocation and emits a single raw mousedown whose effect depends on the current brush. In testDrawErase the multi-step block calls setErase(a) (brush=0) at line ~94 and then invokes paintCell(a,1,1) / paintCell(a,4,5) at lines 99-100 expecting TWO bricks to be drawn. Because the brush is still 0 (erase) AND each paintCell clears the whole board first, bricksOf(a) stays 0, so assert.strictEqual(bricksOf(a),2,...) at line 107 throws AssertionError (0 !== 2). My independent reproduction (.scratch/repro.cjs) reproduces exactly: 'after paint (1,1): 0 null' / 'after paint (4,5): 0 null' and 'EXPECTED 2'. Even when I setDraw() first, the per-call clearGrid() makes bricksOf==1, still short of 2. So the app's editor handlers are correct (draw adds {type:'brick',hp:1,color:'#63b3ed'} at the hit cell -> observed bricks:1 correct:true; erase removes it -> bricks:0) but the test cannot legitimately pass as written.
blockingFindings.evidence: qa/acceptance.cjs lines 99-109 (paintCell helper clears grid each call, leftover erase brush); .scratch/repro.cjs output: 'after paint (1,1): 0 null' / 'after paint (4,5): 0 null'; .scratch/repro2.cjs: 'after draw two WITH setDraw reset: 1 (expect 2)'

blockingFindings.description: The single early throw in testDrawErase aborts the entire main() try/catch (acceptance.cjs main() at line ~327), so checks 2-6 (play_controls, brick_score, lives_game_over, restart_layout, json_roundtrip) never execute and are recorded as failed with empty evidence. This is a cascade effect of the failing test helper, not six independent application defects. The suite's per-check evidence fields are empty precisely because the tests never reached their record() calls.
blockingFindings.evidence: qa/execution.json output: 'at testDrawErase (...acceptance.cjs:107:10) at main (...acceptance.cjs:332:5)'; all six checks passed:false, evidence:'' in qa/acceptance-result.json

residualRisks: The app's real editor behaviour (draw a brick at the pointer cell with the selected color/brush, erase with brush 0, drag to paint, keyboard 0/1 brush switching, play/edit mode toggle, score+10 per brick, life loss, game-over overlay, restart reset, JSON serialize/deserialize roundtrip) could not be fully executed end-to-end because the suite aborts before reaching those checks. I verified the draw and erase atomic operations independently; the remaining behaviors are exercised by code paths that exist and are wired to real handlers but were not run to completion by the failing suite.

The runtime (exact-source Node VM + linkedom + partial Canvas, no browser) cannot run Blob/FileReader downloads synchronously or real requestAnimationFrame loops beyond the instrumented advance(), so some behaviors (live ball physics, save-Blob download) are only partially observable in this environment by design.
I did not modify index.html, acceptance.cjs, or any harness/config; I only added .scratch/*.cjs reproduction scripts.

The failing test helper (paintCell clearing the grid each call + not resetting the brush) is a defect in the acceptance tests, not the artifact; a repair agent should fix the test helper (place bricks without clearing, or set the correct brush) rather than change the application.
